claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To determine your eligibility, I need to start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is your child (or what are the ages of your children)?**

Child Benefit has different eligibility rules depending on the child's age:

- **Under 16**: Generally qualify automatically
- **16-19 years old**: Need to be in full-time education or training
- **20 or over**: Not eligible for Child Benefit

Could you tell me:
1. How many children do you have?
2. What are their ages?
3. What are their names (so I can track them through the assessment)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - my son Alex. He's just turned 18 recently, so I wanted to check if I can still claim for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context! So you have one son, **Alex, who is 18 years old**. That's helpful to know.

Since Alex is 18, he falls into the **16-19 age category**, which means there are additional requirements beyond just his age. Specifically, I need to check whether Alex is in full-time education or approved training.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or an approved training programme?**

This could include:
- Full-time education at a school, college, or university
- An approved apprenticeship or training scheme
- Other government-approved training

Please let me know his current situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education at the moment. He finished school and he's not doing any training or courses right now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex has finished school and is not currently in full-time education or approved training.

Since Alex is 18 years old and **not** in full-time education or approved training, let me navigate through the eligibility rules to determine the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, I can see there's an important question here. Since Alex is not currently in education or training, I need to check whether he **recently left education** (within a certain period), as there may be an extension eligibility available.

**When did Alex finish school?** 

Specifically, how many weeks ago did he leave education? This is important because if he left relatively recently (within a specific timeframe), he may still qualify for Child Benefit under an extension provision.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school a while back now - it's been several months. I'd say around 6 or 7 months ago.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex left school **6-7 months ago**, that's considerably longer than the recent eligibility extension period would typically cover.

Let me check the exact timeframe requirements to be certain:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, I can now see the exact timeframe. According to the rules, there is an **extension period of 20 weeks** for young people who have recently left education. This means they can still qualify for Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks after leaving school.

Since Alex left school **6-7 months ago (approximately 24-28 weeks ago)**, he is **beyond the 20-week extension period**. This means he no longer qualifies for the extension.

Given that:
- Alex is 18 years old
- He is **not** in full-time education or approved training
- He **left education more than 20 weeks ago** (outside the extension period)

Let me navigate to the final determination:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Assessment Result: INELIGIBLE**

Unfortunately, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### **Why?**

Alex is 18 years old and no longer in full-time education or approved training. While there is normally a **20-week grace period** after a young person leaves education during which they can still qualify for Child Benefit, Alex left school **6-7 months ago** — which is **beyond this 20-week extension period**.

### **Key Points:**

- Child Benefit normally stops when a child reaches 16
- **Exception**: If aged 16-19 and in approved full-time education or training, it can continue
- **Additional Exception**: If they leave education, there's a 20-week extension period to allow time to find training or register with careers services
- Alex has now exceeded this 20-week extension, so he no longer qualifies

### **What Happens Next?**

If Alex gets into full-time education or approved training in the future, you would be able to claim again — just make sure to inform HMRC so they can update your claim.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?
